findings.description: New building permits have been issued for an affordable housing infill at 249 Pennsylvania Avenue on Potrero Hill: a nine-story, roughly 108,530-square-foot apartment building with 127 rental units (38 studios, 15 one-bedrooms, 36 two-bedrooms, 35 three-bedrooms) on a vacant lot next to I-280. The developers are the Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation and Young Community Developers; Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects designed it and Suffolk Construction Company is the contractor. The property last sold in 2023 to TNDC for $11.35 million; construction is estimated at $60 million, with a possible 2027 start and 2029 move-ins. No renderings have been released.

extra.developers_of_proposal: Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation and Young Community Developers

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “New Building Permits For 249 Pennsylvania Avenue, San Francisco,” 19 September 2026

raw.text: New building permits have been issued for an affordable housing infill at 249 Pennsylvania Avenue on Potrero Hill, San Francisco.

findings.description: The San Francisco Recovery Fund announced its vision for 50 1st Street in SoMa: 'Fifty at First,' a proposed 915-foot, 56-story, 1.5-million-square-foot office tower on the mothballed Oceanwide Center pit, where construction ceased in 2020. BXP will serve as development, leasing and marketing consultant and JLL as exclusive office leasing agent; Gensler is the architect, with landscape by Field Operations. Permits had not been published at the report; the team hopes to open as early as 2031. If built, it would be the city's second-tallest building.
